text: Two ideal polyatomic gases at temperatures $T_{1}$ and $T_{2}$ are mixed so that there is no loss of energy. If $F_{1}$ and $F_{2}, m_{1}$ and $m_{2}, n_{1}$ and $n_{2}$ be the degrees of freedom, masses, number of molecules of the first and second gas respectively, the temperature of mixture of these two gases is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Initial internal energy = Final internal energy

$\frac{F_{1}}{2}n_{1}RT_{1}+\frac{F_{2}}{2}n_{2}RT_{2}=\frac{F_{1}}{2}n_{1}RT+\frac{F_{2}}{2}n_{2}RT$

$\Rightarrow$ $T=\frac{F_{1}n_{1}T_{1}+F_{2}n_{2}T_{2}}{F_{1}n_{1}+F_{2}n_{2}}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift

text:
A mass M hangs on a massless rod of length l which rotates at a constant angular frequency. The mass M moves with steady speed in a circular path of constant radius. Assume that the system is in steady circular motion with constant angular velocity $ω$. The angular momentum of M about point A is $L_{A}$ which lies in the positive z direction and the angular momentum of M about point B is $L_{B}$. The correct statement for this system is :


[IMG]
options: $L_{A}$ is constant, both in magnitude and direction
$L_{B}$ is constant in direction with varying magnitude
$L_{B}$ is constant, both in magnitude and direction
$L_{A}$ and $L_{B}$ are both constant in magnitude and direction
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
M moves on a horizontal circle of radius $r$ centred at A with constant speed $v$. The net force on M (tension plus weight) is the centripetal force, directed towards A.

About A: the position vector $⃗{r}_{AM}$ and the velocity $⃗{v}$ both lie in the horizontal plane and are perpendicular, so $⃗{L}_{A}=M⃗{r}_{AM}\times ⃗{v}$ has magnitude $Mrv$ and always points along $+z$. The net force passes through A, so the torque about A is zero, consistent with $⃗{L}_{A}$ being constant in magnitude and direction.

About B: $⃗{r}_{BM}$ lies along the rod (length $l$) and is perpendicular to $⃗{v}$, so $|⃗{L}_{B}|=Mlv$ is constant. But $⃗{L}_{B}$ is perpendicular to the rod BM, which sweeps round the cone, so $⃗{L}_{B}$ turns about the $z$ axis along with the mass. The net force (towards A) does not pass through B, so the torque about B is non-zero and changes the direction of $⃗{L}_{B}$.

So $⃗{L}_{B}$ is constant in magnitude but not in direction, which rules out (B), (C) and (D).

Hence, the correct option is (A).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift

text: The thickness at the centre of a plano-convex lens is 3 mm and the diameter is 6 cm. If the speed of light in the material of the lens is 2 $\times$ $10^{8} ms^{-1}$, the focal length of the lens is $____________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The curved face is part of a sphere of radius $R$. The aperture radius is $3\text{cm}$ and the central thickness is $0.3\text{cm}$, so the right triangle in the figure gives


[IMG]

$R^{2}=3^{2}+(R-0.3)^{2}\Rightarrow 0.6R=9.09\Rightarrow R=15.15\text{cm}$

Refractive index of the lens:

$μ=\dfrac{c}{v}=\dfrac{3\times 10^{8}}{2\times 10^{8}}=1.5$

Lens maker's formula for a plano-convex lens ($R_{1}=R$, $R_{2}=\infty$):

$\dfrac{1}{f}=(μ-1)\dfrac{1}{R}\Rightarrow f=\dfrac{15.15}{0.5}=30.3\text{cm}\approx 30\text{cm}$

Hence, the correct option is (B).

text:
The output of the given combination gates represents :


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In each of the first two NOR gates both inputs are joined, so each acts as a NOT gate and their outputs are $\bar{A}$ and $\bar{B}$.

The middle NOR gate gives

$\bar{A}+\bar{B}–=A\cdot B$

by De Morgan's theorem.

The last NOR gate also has its inputs joined and acts as a NOT gate, so

$Y=A\cdot B–$

which is the NAND function ($Y=0$ only when $A=B=1$).

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text:
Four identical rectangular plates with length, l = 2 cm and breadth, b = $\frac{3}{2}$ cm are arranged as shown in figure. The equivalent capacitance between A and C is $\frac{xε_{0}}{d}$. The value of x is $______________. ($Round off to the Nearest Integer)


[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Each pair of facing plates forms a capacitor $C=\dfrac{ε_{0}A}{d}$ with $A=lb=2\times \dfrac{3}{2}=3\text{cm}^{2}$.

A and B form one capacitor $C$. B and D are joined, so the capacitors B-C and D-C both lie between the joined plates and C and are in parallel: $2C$.

Between A and C these are in series:

$C_{eq}=\dfrac{C\times 2C}{C+2C}=\dfrac{2C}{3}=\dfrac{2}{3}\times \dfrac{3~ε_{0}}{d}=\dfrac{2~ε_{0}}{d}$

Here $x$ carries the unit of area and the plate dimensions are in cm, so $x=2$ (that is, $2\text{cm}^{2}$).

Hence, the answer is 2.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift

text: The equivalent resistance of series combination of two resistors is 's'. When they are connected in parallel, the equivalent resistance is 'p'. If s = np, then the minimum value for n is $____________. ($Round off to the Nearest Integer)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$s=np$

$R_{1}+R_{2}=n\left [\frac{R_{1}R_{2}}{R_{1}+R_{2}}\right ]$

$\Rightarrow$ $R_{1}^{2}+R_{2}^{2}+2R_{1}R_{2}=nR_{1}R_{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $R_{1}^{2}+(2-n)R_{1}R_{2}+R_{2}^{2}=0$

For real roots, $b^{2} - 4ac$ $\geq$ 0

 $[(2-n)R_{2}]^{2}-4\times 1\times R_{2}^{2}$ $\geq$ 0

$\Rightarrow$ $(2-n)^{2}R_{2}^{2}\geq 4R_{2}^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ 2 $-$ n $\geq\pm$2

$\Rightarrow$ 2 $-$ n $\geq$ $-$2

$\Rightarrow$ n $\geq$ 4

 So, minimum value for n = 4
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 17th March Morning Shift
